prompt: A robot takes laps. What is printed, in order?

options.text: `beep` then `done`. The body runs one time in total.
options.feedback: A loop runs its body once per lap: range(2) gives two laps, so beep is printed twice before done. Next step: follow the loop lap by lap.

options.text: `beep` then `done` then `beep` then `done`. done belongs to the loop.
options.feedback: done sits outside the loop — its indentation puts it after the loop, not in the body. Next step: match each print to the indentation that owns it.

options.text: `beep` then `beep` then `done`. Only the first indented line repeats.
options.feedback: The output here is right, but every indented line repeats: with print("stamp") added under the for, a real run gives beep, stamp, beep, stamp, done.
options.partial_reason: Correct: two beeps and one done here. Incorrect: that only the first indented line repeats; all indented lines run on every lap.

options.text: `beep` then `beep` then `done`. One beep per lap; done runs once.
options.feedback: Correct. range(2) gives two laps, the body prints beep on each, and done comes once when the loop has finished.

explanation: range(2) gives two laps (turns 0 and 1). The indented print("beep") runs once per lap, so beep appears twice. print("done") is not indented, so it runs a single time after the loop.
